destinations.name: Basilica del Santo Niño
destinations.location: Cebu City Downtown, near Magellan's Cross
destinations.travel_style: Cultural Trip Sightseeing & reflection
destinations.description: The oldest Roman Catholic church in the Philippines, home to the revered Santo Niño statue and a cornerstone of Cebuano faith.
overview: The Basilica Minore del Santo Niño de Cebú is a minor basilica in Cebu City dedicated to the Santo Niño (Holy Child Jesus). It is the oldest Roman Catholic church established in the Philippines, founded in 1565.

The basilica houses the image of the Santo Niño, a gift from Ferdinand Magellan to Rajah Humabon's wife, Queen Juana, upon their baptism in 1521. Today, it is a major pilgrimage site and the center of the annual Sinulog Festival.
Visitors can attend mass, light a candle in the outdoor candle lighting area, or visit the small museum that houses religious artifacts and historical items.

overview: Magellan's Cross is a Christian cross planted by Portuguese and Spanish explorers, as ordered by Ferdinand Magellan, upon arriving in Cebu in the Philippines on April 21, 1521.

destinations.name: Fort San Pedro
destinations.travel_style: Quick Stop Usually 30-60 mins
destinations.description: A historic Spanish military fort built in 1738, now a peaceful garden and museum in the heart of Cebu City.
overview: Fuerte de San Pedro, or Fort San Pedro, is a military defense structure built by the Spanish under the command of Miguel López de Legazpi. It is the oldest triangular bastion fort in the Philippines.
Originally built of wood in 1565, it was later replaced by a stone structure in 1738 to repel Muslim raiders. Over the centuries, it served as a military barracks, a prison, and even a zoo.

Today, it is a peaceful walled garden featuring a small museum that houses Spanish artifacts, paintings, and documents. The fort offers a quiet escape from the bustling city and beautiful views of the port.

destinations.name: Malapascua Island
destinations.description: A quiet island in northern Cebu famous for daily thresher shark dives, vibrant coral reefs, and beautiful white-sand beaches.
overview: Malapascua Island is a small, peaceful island located off the northern tip of Cebu in Daanbantayan. It is world-renowned among divers for being one of the only places on Earth where you can reliably see thresher sharks in their natural habitat.

The thresher sharks come to the nearby Monad Shoal, a sunken island, every morning to be cleaned by small reef fish. Aside from the sharks, the island offers beautiful white-sand beaches, vibrant coral reefs, and a laid-back atmosphere.
Getting there involves a scenic 3.5 to 4-hour bus ride from Cebu City to Maya Port, followed by a short 30-minute boat ride to the island.
destinations.operating_hours: from Cebu City

transportation.details: 🚌 Bus to Maya Port 3.5 - 4 hrs From Cebu North Bus Terminal, take a Ceres bus bound for Maya Port in Daanbantayan. The bus ride is scenic and passes through several towns.
🚤 Boat to Malapascua 30 mins From Maya Port, take a local outrigger boat (bangka) to Malapascua Island. Boats run regularly during daylight hours.

visitor_tips: Thresher shark dives require an early start, usually leaving at 4:30 AM to reach the shoal by sunrise. If you are not a diver, you can still enjoy snorkeling, island hopping, and relaxing on the beautiful beaches.

destinations.name: Moalboal Sardine Run
destinations.description: Experience millions of sardines and sea turtles just meters from the shore in this vibrant coastal town on Cebu's south-west coast.
overview: Moalboal sits on Cebu's south-west coast, about 90 km from Cebu City. Its sardine run is one of the Philippines' most famous marine attractions — you can snorkel right near the shore without needing a boat.

Green sea turtles are often spotted in the same coastal waters, feeding in the seagrass beds. Most travellers visit for a day trip or an overnight stay, combining the sardine run and sea turtles with a Pescador Island boat tour.

The drive from Cebu City usually takes around 2.5–3 hours by private car. Public buses can take longer because of traffic and stops along the route. Some travellers also visit Kawasan Falls for canyoneering farther south.

destinations.name: Oslob Whale Sharks
destinations.location: Oslob, Cebu Southern tip of Cebu
destinations.description: Swim alongside the gentle giants of the sea in the clear waters of southern Cebu—an unforgettable marine encounter.
overview: Oslob is a coastal town in southern Cebu famous for its whale shark interaction. Locally known as "butanding," these gentle giants gather in the waters off Barangay Tan-awan, where locals feed them small shrimp.

While the practice is controversial among conservationists, it has become a major tourist draw. The activity is tightly regulated: you must watch a briefing, wear a life vest, and keep a safe distance (at least 4 meters) from the sharks.
Beyond the whale sharks, Oslob is also home to the stunning Tumalog Falls and the historic Cuartel Ruins, making it a great day trip or overnight destination.

overview: Osmeña Peak is the highest mountain in Cebu, standing at 1,013 meters above sea level. It is located in the town of Dalaguete, about 2.5 to 3 hours from Cebu City.
The peak is famous for its unique landscape of rolling, jagged hills that resemble the Chocolate Hills of Bohol. From the summit, you can see a stunning panorama of the coastline and the sea.
The hike to the peak is relatively easy, usually taking about 15 to 20 minutes from the jump-off point. Many visitors come here for sunrise or sunset, camping, and photography.

destinations.description: A grand, castle-like church that serves as a major pilgrimage site in southern Cebu, known for its miraculous image of the Virgin Mary.
overview: The Monastery of the Holy Eucharist, commonly known as Simala Shrine, is a grand, castle-like church located in Sibonga, southern Cebu. It is one of the most popular pilgrimage sites in the Philippines.

The shrine is home to a miraculous image of the Virgin Mary, and it is believed to grant miracles and heal the sick. The architecture is stunning, with towering spires, intricate details, and beautifully landscaped gardens.
Visitors can attend mass, light candles, offer prayers, and explore the shrine grounds. It is a place of deep spiritual significance for many Filipinos.

overview: Sumilon Island is a 24-hectare coral island located off the southeastern tip of Cebu in Oslob. It is best known for its shifting sandbar—a stretch of white sand that changes shape depending on the tide and the season.
The island is also a protected marine sanctuary, making it a fantastic spot for snorkeling and diving. The waters around the island are teeming with vibrant coral and diverse marine life.
You don't need to stay at the luxury resort (Bluewater Sumilon) to visit. Day-trippers can take a short boat ride from the mainland to enjoy the sandbar and snorkeling area.

overview: Tumalog Falls is a breathtaking waterfall located in Oslob, southern Cebu. It is famous for its unique "curtain" style—the water cascades down a wide, moss-covered rock face, creating a fine mist that cools the area.
The pool at the base of the falls is shallow and refreshing, making it a great spot for swimming and relaxing. The surrounding area is lush and green, with towering trees and tropical plants.
Because it is just a short drive from the whale shark watching area in Tan-awan, many visitors combine the two activities in a single day trip.
